## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sattalipupphapūjakattheraapadāna* is a short biographical verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali canon [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. Belonging to the genre of Apadāna literature, it recounts the past karmic deed of an elder who offered *sattalī* flowers to an earlier Buddha and subsequently experienced favorable rebirths before attaining arahantship [Catalog]. The text is cataloged as Tha Ap 250, and SuttaCentral records five modern translations across five languages [SuttaCentral].
No direct external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal formulaic reuse with other *Therāpadāna* compositions involving floral offerings. It shares passages (notably across segments §1.1–5.1) with poems such as the *Campakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 348), *Naḷinakesariyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 245), *Pāṭalipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 374), and *Kesarapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 366), demonstrating the standardized conventional phrasing characteristic of the collection [DharmaNexus].
